subject: Is there a three level hierarchical model in unmarked suitable for this type of counts?

messages.author: cf45c6aa992bbacc
messages.subject: Is there a three level hierarchical model in unmarked suitable for this type of counts?
parts:
Dear All,

We are trying to develop a hierarchical model to fit a specific kind of data. We thought that some existing function in unmarked might do the work but until now we have not been able to do that.
Here it is as our data look like. We have a number of sites (i) that are surveyed by multiple observers (j) over a number of sessions (t). At least for the moment we want to assume that the superpopulation size (M) of individuals susceptible of being available in a certain site is constant among sessions, Mi~Poisson(λ). However the number of individuals available to be detected at each session can change throughout the t sessions so that Nit~Binomial(Mi,φit). We need to account for the possibility that φ changes over time t and space i. For several reasons we cannot use the classical robust design approach with secondary occasions so we think we may estimate the detection probability by using multiple observers at each session t. In some sense the secondary occasions would be replaced by multiple observers. So, by calling y the number of counted individuals would be:  yijt~Binomial(Nit,pit). In other words we would be assuming that the detection probability p does not vary as a function of the observer j but uniquely as a function of time t and space i.

Our parameter of main interest is f. We want to investigate how this parameter changes across sites and over time.

Is there any existing function in unmarked that might be accommodated to fit this data type?
We tried with gmultmix but it seems to us that, even if it includes the possibility of multiple observers, it always requires secondary occasions.
Any help would be really appreciated.
Best,

Simone
